title: The supported lifted object detects zero on the smaller localized open
statement: Let $X$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] with derived localizations for module sheaves and their open restrictions [def-pc-derived-category]. Let $s$ be a finite affine open cover with $|s|\geq2$. Assume that for each scheme with the same hypotheses and a strictly smaller finite affine cover, every closed subset with quasi-compact complement has a perfect supported zero detector in its quasi-coherent derived category [def-pc-perfect-complex]. For a closed $T\subseteq X$ with quasi-compact complement, there exist a quasi-compact open $U$, an affine open $V$ with $U\cup V=X$, a right adjoint $R$ and adjunction $L\dashv R$ for derived restriction $L$ to the localized module site over $U$, and a perfect quasi-coherent $Q$ supported on $T$, such that for each quasi-coherent $K$ supported on $T$, vanishing of $\operatorname{Hom}(L(Q[n]),L(K))$ for every integer $n$ implies $L(K)=0$. Support means vanishing of every cohomology stalk outside $T$. This conclusion only asserts vanishing on $U$.

proof.text: Choose V in s, let a=s.erase V and U be its finite union. Compactness follows from Finset.isCompact_biUnion and compactness of affine opens. The cover identity gives U union V=X. Pull each remaining affine chart back to U; because it lies inside U, IsAffineOpen.preimage_of_isOpenImmersion applies. Form the image Finset t. card_image_le and card_erase_lt_of_mem give t.card<s.card. The induced cover is checked pointwise. Compactness and quasi-separatedness of U follow from the subtype compactness and open-embedding APIs. For S=Subtype.val inverse-image T, closedness is by continuity; compactness of its complement follows from compactness of U intersect T-complement and Subtype.isCompact_iff.

Apply [lem-pc-open-derived-restriction-comparison] to get the open localizations, R and adj and restriction comparisons. Apply the given ih directly to U, t and S, obtaining the perfect supported detector P.

Construct the actual zero quasi-coherent derived object from the free module on PEmpty and additive homology. Apply [lem-sc-perfect-support-map-lift] to P and the zero map. This gives a perfect global Q supported on T and maps i and p with i composed with p equal to the identity of P. For each open, the comparison theorem supplies the localization needed to apply [lem-pc-perfect-pseudo-coherent-locally-finite-tor]. Its first conclusion and [lem-sc-pseudo-coherent-qcoh] give quasi-coherent cohomology of Q.

For a supported quasi-coherent K, use the comparison to equip M(K) with quasi-coherence and support. The shifted Hom comparison turns the given orthogonality into subsingleton Hom(M(Q)[n],M(K)). Apply the shift functor to i and p; functoriality preserves their retract equation. For maps b,c from P[n], subsingletonness gives p[n] composed with b equal to p[n] composed with c; precompose by i[n] and cancel the retract identity to obtain b=c. The detector P makes M(K) zero, and reflection of zero gives L(K) zero.

theorem exists_supported_detector_open_lift_core
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))]
    [∀ U : X.Opens,
      HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U))]
    (s : Finset X.affineOpens) (hcover : (⨆ U ∈ s, (U : X.Opens)) = ⊤)
    (hcard : 2 ≤ s.card)
    (ih : ∀ (Y : Scheme.{u}) [CompactSpace Y] [QuasiSeparatedSpace Y]
      [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace))]
      [∀ U : Y.Opens,
        HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace).over U))]
      (t : Finset Y.affineOpens), t.card < s.card →
      (⨆ U ∈ t, (U : Y.Opens)) = ⊤ →
      ∀ (S : Set Y), IsClosed S → IsCompact Sᶜ →
        ∃ E : schemeDerivedQCohCategory Y, Scheme.IsPerfect Y E.obj ∧
          (∀ (n : ℤ) (x : Y), x ∉ S →
            Subsingleton (↑(TopCat.Presheaf.stalk ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
              (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace)) n).obj E.obj).val.presheaf x))) ∧
          ∀ K : schemeDerivedQCohCategory Y,
            (∀ (n : ℤ) (x : Y), x ∉ S →
              Subsingleton (↑(TopCat.Presheaf.stalk ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
                (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace)) n).obj K.obj).val.presheaf x))) →
            (∀ n : ℤ, Subsingleton (E.obj⟦n⟧ ⟶ K.obj)) → IsZero K.obj)
    (T : Set X) (hT : IsClosed T) (hTc : IsCompact Tᶜ) :
    ∃ (U : X.Opens) (V : X.affineOpens), IsCompact (U : Set X) ∧
      U ⊔ (V : X.Opens) = ⊤ ∧
      ∃ (R : DerivedCategory
          (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U)) ⥤
          schemeDerivedCategory X)
        (adj : (SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u}
          (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) U).mapDerivedCategory ⊣ R)
        (Q : schemeDerivedQCohCategory X),
        Scheme.IsPerfect X Q.obj ∧
        (∀ (n : ℤ) (x : X), x ∉ T →
          Subsingleton (↑(TopCat.Presheaf.stalk ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
            (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) n).obj Q.obj).val.presheaf x))) ∧
        ∀ K : schemeDerivedQCohCategory X,
          (∀ (n : ℤ) (x : X), x ∉ T →
            Subsingleton (↑(TopCat.Presheaf.stalk ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
              (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) n).obj K.obj).val.presheaf x))) →
          (∀ n : ℤ, Subsingleton
            ((SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) U).mapDerivedCategory.obj
               (Q.obj⟦n⟧) ⟶
            (SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) U).mapDerivedCategory.obj
               K.obj)) →
          IsZero
            ((SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) U).mapDerivedCategory.obj
               K.obj)
